text: Vessels and tonics, one wall each, stacked to the ceiling.
A city shop, and it is stocked like one: nothing is rationed
and nobody is counting what you take.
Working gear. Boots, lamps, oilskins, and a rack of pick handles
worn smooth at one end by people who did not buy them here.
The Hall shelf: everything a challenger comes back down wanting,
arranged in the order they usually want it.
Potions first. Then rope. Then, apparently, biscuits.
A pot plant that has been fed shop tea for six years and thrived on it.
There is a small sign on the pot with its name on.
A price board, chalked, with a second column headed QUARRY.
Every number in the second column is lower.
Nobody checks whether you work there. That is the whole system.
